parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Aries, the Ram, is a constellation of stars

explanation.surface: An astronomer laments that the stars have been caught in a state of decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is the medical word for tooth or bone decay.

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a strain is a breed or race of animal or plant

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect something before a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: We prosper with engineering drawing in university in dominant country

indicators.note: drawing in means pulling something inside, so the shuffled letters close round the next piece
engineering means contriving or reworking, so the letters of we prosper are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nation boasts that, thanks to engineering and its universities, it has become the dominant country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'engineering' rearranges WE PROSPER, and 'drawing in' places U inside that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A superpower is a nation of overwhelming global influence, so a dominant country.

clue.text: Varied choice essential in popular sport in Canada etc

indicators.note: varied means altered, so the letters of choice are reordered

parts.note: key as an adjective means essential or crucial

explanation.surface: A varied choice is essential if a sport is to be popular in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: The game on ice with sticks and a puck is a national passion in Canada and played elsewhere too.

clue.text: In a frenzy 'Good Morning' the wrong way round

indicators.note: the wrong way round says the two parts of the greeting are put in the opposite order

parts.note: OK means good or acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone greets the day by saying 'Good Morning' back to front, as if in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: The greeting's two words swap places, not their letters: AM comes first, then OK.
explanation.definitionFit: To run amok is to behave wildly and uncontrollably, so it describes being in a frenzy.

indicators.note: written in says one letter is inserted into the middle of another word

parts.note: coral is a pinkish-orange colour
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: The Queen has signed her name in pink ink.
explanation.definitionFit: A corral is an enclosure for livestock, which is what a pen is.

clue.text: Changing hat style not likely to be noticed

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters of hat style are rearranged

explanation.surface: Changing one's hat style is not likely to be noticed by anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy behaviour is furtive and quiet, designed to escape attention.

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the planet's name surrounds the letter for Earth

parts.note: Venus is the second planet from the sun

explanation.surface: An astronomical scene of a planet orbiting Earth as it draws closer.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenues are ways in or routes towards something, as in avenues of inquiry or approaches.

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, so in a down entry the word is read backwards

parts.note: Macs are the computers made by Apple

explanation.surface: A fraud has left owners of Apple computers upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme to cheat people, a synonym for a fraud.

clue.text: Become apparent as the Witham, Welland, Nene and Great Ouse do

definitions.meaning: the idiom means to be revealed eventually

definitions.text: the Witham, Welland, Nene and Great Ouse do
definitions.meaning: these four English rivers all empty into the Wash, the large bay on the coast of Lincolnshire and Norfolk

explanation.surface: A geography note on what four eastern English rivers have in common.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a broad square bay on England's east coast; the idiom literally describes where these rivers emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says a truth will surface in the end, just as dirt shows up in laundry.

clue.text: Country that was divided making progress rapidly, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for rushing is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: to career is to rush along at speed

explanation.surface: A nation that was once split apart is now making rapid progress, we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula was split into North and South after the Second World War.

definitions.meaning: to frank a letter is to mark it to show postage has been paid
to bring one's foot down heavily on the ground

explanation.surface: A man called Frank firmly put his foot down.
explanation.definitionFit: Franking marks postage on mail, and stomping brings a foot down hard; one word does both.

parts.note: a chap is a man
to let is to allow or permit

explanation.surface: A man applies for a licence to lay a wreath.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a garland or circlet of flowers worn on the head.

clue.text: Old actress gives former UN chief the bird

parts.note: Kofi Annan was Secretary-General of the United Nations
the eagle is a large bird of prey

explanation.surface: A veteran actress is handed a bird by an ex-head of the United Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Anna Neagle was a leading British film star of the 1930s to 1950s.

clue.text: Bag to boil for cooking that is required for musicians

indicators.note: cooking means fiddling or doctoring, so the letters of bag to boil are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for boil-in-the-bag food that are obligatory for musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'that is' are links; the definition is 'required for musicians'.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian term marks an accompanying part that must be played, not omitted.

clue.text: What's green lawyer been spinning? Alternative sources of power

indicators.note: spinning means whirling round, so the letters of green lawyer been are mixed up

explanation.surface: Asking what an environmentally minded lawyer has been spinning about green power.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind, solar and tidal power are alternatives to fossil fuels that never run out.

clue.text: Everyday existence is prevalent, engrossing English entirely

indicators.note: engrossing means absorbing, so the word for prevalent takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: rife means widespread or prevalent
all means wholly or entirely

explanation.surface: A sentence about English being dominant everywhere in ordinary life.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary day-to-day living, as opposed to fiction or fantasy, is what the phrase describes.

indicators.note: in says the word for following someone sits inside the plant

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like waterside plant
to tail someone is to follow or dog them

explanation.surface: A dog was sold after being found in a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To retail goods is to sell them to the public, so retailed means sold.

indicators.note: in says the army corps goes inside the word for dismay

parts.note: to appal is to horrify or dismay
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers are dismayed by the equipment they have been given.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is clothing, and gear is an informal word for clothes.

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
fab was 1960s slang for great or fabulous

explanation.surface: A nostalgic description of a building style before the swinging sixties.
explanation.definitionFit: Factory-built homes were put up quickly in Britain after the Second World War to replace bombed housing.

clue.text: Bits of music jumping from las to dohs?

definitions.text: Bits of music jumping from las to dohs?

parts.words: Bits of music jumping from las to dohs
parts.note: la and doh are names of steps on the sol-fa scale, so moving between them is a jump between musical pitches

explanation.surface: Fragments of a tune leaping between steps of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.walkthrough: La and doh are syllables of the tonic sol-fa scale, so the plural names stand for single pitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sung pitch, such as la or doh, is one of the written symbols of music.

clue.text: Goblin shows ill will without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for malice wraps round the letter

parts.note: spite is malice or ill will
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A mischievous goblin behaves spitefully but offers no resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like it means minus, but here it means outside, so SPITE goes around R rather than losing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf or fairy, a small supernatural creature like a goblin.

definitions.meaning: the dining hall where officers or soldiers eat together
British slang, from the malted drink, for a muddle or botched job

explanation.surface: Soldiers drink a malted milk drink in their dining quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Horlicks is a British malted bedtime drink; 'to make a Horlicks of something' is slang for making a botch of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The military dining room and a shambles share the same short word.

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A clingy acquaintance is offered sanctuary by the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a parasite, figuratively a person who clings on for their own gain.

definitions.meaning: in American English the engine cover of a car, which Britons call the bonnet, has a different name
US slang, short for hoodlum, a thug or criminal

explanation.surface: A car part for an American mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: The US word for a car bonnet is also slang for a hoodlum or gangster.

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of dearer gin are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier has drunk gin that was more expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadiers are infantry soldiers, originally those who threw grenades.

clue.text: Ignore rules going round a kind of junction as fast as possible

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the word for ignoring rules surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to flout rules is to ignore them openly
a T-junction is where one road meets another at right angles

explanation.surface: A reckless driver ignores the rules at a road junction while going at top speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Going all out, at maximum speed, is a common idiom.

clue.text: Where yachtsmen sail, keeping very well-funded

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the stretch of water holds the letter inside it

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England, famous for yachting

explanation.surface: Yachting waters remain the playground of the very wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the channel off southern England that hosts Cowes Week, a famous sailing regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: Being solvent means having enough money to pay one's debts.
